# Intake Brief: ship — `run-release.js --help` runs post-release steps against a stale tag

## Goal (user story)

As a release operator, when I pass an unsupported flag (e.g. `--help`) to the
ship release wrapper, I want the wrapper to **fail fast with usage** and make
**no** git, worklog, notification, or close-side-effects, so that a mistaken or
exploratory invocation can never close release-ready work items without a real
`dev` → `main` merge.

## Problem statement

`node $(skill_path ship)/scripts/run-release.js --help` did not print wrapper
help. Instead it ran the entire post-release tail of the wrapper:

- it forwarded `--help` to the canonical merge script
  (`scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`), which printed its own usage and
  exited `0` **without merging**;
- Step 8 then read the *latest existing* tag via
  `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` (returning the already-shipped `v0.1.18`);
- `verifyReleaseMerge('0.1.18')` **passed** because that tag already exists on
  `origin/main` and is an ancestor of it;
- the wrapper therefore sent a Discord release notification and ran
  `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease('0.1.18')`.

Observed on 2026-10-09 (project `tce-main-street`, dev 72 commits ahead of
main, no merge performed): **98 work items were spuriously closed** (152 close
comments — 150 `Closed with reason: Shipped in v0.1.18` plus 2 cascade
comments). The worklog was subsequently restored to its exact pre-incident
state (0 item-state diffs, 0 extra/missing comments) from the full worklog
snapshot `588ff39` + delta `e7357f3`.

## Root causes

1. `releaseScriptForwardArgs()` strips only documented wrapper-only flags
   (`--skip-checks`, `--refresh-audits`, `--skip-audit-remediation`) and
   forwards everything else — including `--help`/`-h`/unknown flags — to the
   merge script.
2. A merge-script exit `0` is treated as a successful release regardless of
   whether a new tag/merge was produced.
3. Merge verification keys off `git describe` (the newest *reachable* tag),
   which can be an old, already-released tag, so it does not prove *this* run
   produced a release.

## Acceptance criteria

- `run-release.js --help` and `run-release.js -h` print wrapper usage and exit without invoking any gate, merge script, `wl`, git-mutation, Discord notification, or close command.
- An unrecognised flag causes a non-zero exit with usage text; unknown flags are never silently forwarded to the merge script.
- Post-release steps (Discord notification, `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`) run only when the released version tag was **newly created by this run** (did not exist before the run) and its commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`.
- Regression test: with `--help` and with a bogus flag, asserts zero side effects (no `wl close`, no `sendReleaseNotification`, no merge subprocess).
- A merge-script invocation that exits `0` without producing a new tag is detected and does not run post-release steps.

## Evidence

- Incident window comments: 2026-10-09T07:36:05–07:36:10Z, author `worklog`
  (`Closed with reason: Shipped in v0.1.18`) and author `ship` (cascade).
- Pre-incident snapshot ref: `refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data`
  full `588ff39` + delta `e7357f3` (2026-10-09T07:34Z).
- `origin/main` stayed at `eebde87`; no `release/*` branch or new tag created.

## Constraints

- Must not weaken merge verification; the fix must be strictly more
  conservative.
- Preserve the existing documented flag set and behaviour for the normal
  no-arg release path.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MRHQC1SJ007WLBW** – Add critical-priority item gating to ship skill release process (completed)
- **SA-0MQJIL0KK003BO55** – Implement: ready_to_merge stage in workflow (completed)
- **SA-0MSGN5OJ4002OZKY** – Cache full test-suite results for reuse across ship/audit/implement workflows (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: acceptance, already, ancestor, arg, audit (+145 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: acceptance, already, ancestor, arg, asserts (+140 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: abbrev, ahead, already, ancestor, arg (+124 more)

data.description:
# Intake Brief: ship — release announcement (Discord) sent without a completed release

## Goal (user story)

As a release operator, I want the post-release Discord announcement to be sent
**only** after a release has verifiably landed on `main` — i.e. a version tag
that this run **newly created** and that is an ancestor of `origin/main` — so
that the project channel is never told a release shipped when none did.

## Problem statement

On 2026-10-09 a release announcement for `v0.1.18` was posted to the project
Discord even though **no `dev` → `main` merge occurred** and no new release was
cut. `v0.1.18` had already shipped on 2026-10-06; the run created no new tag.
The announcement is externally visible and cannot be retracted.

## Root cause analysis (RCA)

Event chain:

1. `run-release.js` was invoked with `--help` (a diagnostic). The wrapper
   forwards unknown flags to the canonical merge script
   (the canonical merge script; in this repository `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`), which printed its usage and exited
   `0` **without merging**.
2. Because the merge script exited `0`, the wrapper continued to the
   post-release steps.
3. Step 8 resolved the "released version" via
   `git describe --tags --abbrev=0`, which returns the newest **reachable** tag —
   the already-shipped `v0.1.18` — not a tag produced by this run.
4. `verifyReleaseMerge('0.1.18')` returned success because `v0.1.18` genuinely
   exists on `origin/main` and is an ancestor of it.
5. `sendReleaseNotification({ version: '0.1.18', ... })` posted the announcement.

Contributing root causes:

- **R1 — No argument validation.** Unknown / `--help` flags are forwarded to the
  merge script instead of being rejected by the wrapper.
- **R2 — Merge success inferred from exit code only.** A merge-script exit `0`
  is treated as a completed release with no assertion that a new tag/merge was
  produced.
- **R3 — Version derived from "newest reachable tag".** `git describe` conflates
  *this run's* release with the latest pre-existing release.
- **R4 — `verifyReleaseMerge` proves existence, not provenance.** It proves the
  tag exists on `origin/main`; it does not prove this run created it.
- **R5 — Notification guarded only by R4's result.** There is no independent
  check that the announcement corresponds to a release produced by the run.

Impact: an irreversible external announcement for a release that did not happen.
The same root defect also produced 98 spurious work-item closes (filed
separately as SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR).

## Acceptance criteria

1. The notification is sent only when the version tag was **newly created during
   this run** (the tag did not exist before the run) **and** is an ancestor of
   `origin/main`; otherwise no announcement is sent.
2. The wrapper captures the pre-run tag set (or pre-run `HEAD`/tag) and aborts
   the post-release steps if the merge script exits `0` without producing a new
   version tag.
3. `--help`/unknown flags cause a non-zero exit with usage and run no
   post-release steps (shared requirement with SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR).
4. Regression test: a run in which the merge script exits `0` without a new tag
   asserts that no Discord POST is performed.
5. Defence in depth: `sendReleaseNotification` independently refuses to send
   when the resolved version's tag was not created by the current run.

## Evidence

- Wrapper log line: `Discord release notification sent for v0.1.18.`
- `origin/main` remained at `eebde87`; the only tag is `v0.1.18` (created
  2026-10-06); no `release/*` branch was created.
- Spurious close comments at 2026-10-09T07:36Z.

## Related

- SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR — same root defect (spurious closes from `--help`).
## Minimal Implementation

- Snapshot the pre-run tag set (`git tag --list`) **before** invoking the merge
  script and use it as the provenance baseline for this run.
- After the merge script exits `0`, resolve the released version from a tag that
  was **newly created during this run** (absent from the pre-run snapshot)
  instead of `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` (which returns the newest
  *reachable* tag); refuse the post-release steps and exit non-zero when no new
  tag was produced.
- In `sendReleaseNotification`, accept the pre-run tag set (or a
  `tagCreatedByThisRun` flag) and return
  `{ success: true, notified: false, reason: 'version tag not created by this run' }`
  **before** resolving the webhook or building the payload, so no POST is ever
  attempted (AC5 defence in depth).
- Keep `verifyReleaseMerge(version)` (tag exists on origin + ancestor of
  `origin/main`) as an additional gate; no existing check is weakened.
- Document the notifier contract change in `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`
  only if the exported signature changes.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` (Step 8 verify, Step 8.5 notification)
- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` (`sendReleaseNotification`)
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs`
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-merge-guard.mjs`

## Reuse & related work

The sibling tree **SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR** plans the wrapper-side fixes for the
same root defect; reuse it rather than duplicating work:

- **SA-0MV13B5WO008CYXA** — *Gate post-release steps on a newly created tag*:
  implements the wrapper-side pre-run tag snapshot and refusal (AC2, and AC1
  end-to-end). This item depends on it.
- **SA-0MV13B4YT0093CKT** — *Regression tests: fail-fast flags and stale-tag
  gating*: supplies the wrapper-level regression harness (temp skill layout,
  mocked `git`/`wl`/`gh`, recording merge script) and already asserts no
  `sendReleaseNotification` on stale-tag runs. Reuse as the model for AC4 and
  enforce test-first ordering. This item depends on it.
- **SA-0MV13B5F8005NT6G** — *Fail-fast CLI argument handling in run-release.js*:
  implements AC3 (shared requirement); owned there, not duplicated here.

Unique to this item (not covered by the sibling tree): **AC5** — an independent
provenance guard inside `sendReleaseNotification` so the notifier itself
refuses to send when the resolved version's tag was not created by the current
run.

**OPEN QUESTION** (directed to: producer, blocks scope certainty) — AC1, AC2
and AC4 overlap with the sibling items above. Should this item (a) be limited
to the notifier-side defence-in-depth (AC5) plus the Discord-specific
regression test, depending on the sibling fixes; or (b) own the full
end-to-end fix and have the sibling items deduplicated against it? Planning
assumes **(a)** and wires the dependencies accordingly; if (b) is preferred,
the sibling items must be reconciled before implementation starts.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MV13B5F8005NT6G** – Fail-fast CLI argument handling in run-release.js (blocked)
- **SA-0MQH8CPCD00250DR** – Documentation & Verification (completed)
- **SA-0MU7K9FJS0023L2J** – [test-failure] TestScopePropagated::test_run_suite_carries_scope — failing test (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: aborts, acceptance, already, also, analysis (+118 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: aborts, acceptance, already, also, analysis (+104 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: abbrev, already, also, ancestor, argument (+96 more)

# Regression tests: fail-fast flags and stale-tag gating

Test-first (TDD red baseline) for the `run-release.js` fail-fast and
newly-created-tag fixes. Extends the existing `tests/unit/test-run-release-*.mjs`
family.

## Goal (user story)

As a release operator, I want regression tests that pin the wrapper's
fail-fast behaviour for `--help`/unknown flags and its refusal to run
post-release steps against a stale tag, so the 2026-10-09 spurious-close
incident cannot silently recur.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Regression tests assert zero side effects for `--help`/`-h` (exit 0, wrapper usage text) and with a bogus flag (non-zero exit, wrapper usage text): no `wl close`, no `sendReleaseNotification`, and no merge subprocess.
- A test invokes the wrapper with a merge script that exits `0` without producing a new tag and asserts no post-release steps run.
- Tests reuse the existing temp-skill-layout pattern with mocked `git`, `wl` and `gh` and a recording merge script.
- Tests fail against the current implementation and pass once the fail-fast and newly-created-tag fixes land.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `tests/unit/test-run-release-fail-fast.mjs`, modelled on `test-run-release-arg-filtering.mjs` and `test-run-release-merge-guard.mjs`.
- `--help`/`-h`: assert exit 0, wrapper usage text, empty recording-merge-script file, and no `wl`/close/notification side effects.
- Bogus flag (e.g. `--nope`): assert non-zero exit, usage text, and empty recording-merge-script file.
- Merge script exits 0 without a new tag: assert non-zero wrapper exit and no close/notification.
- Run with `node --test tests/unit/test-run-release-fail-fast.mjs`.

**Key Files:**
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-fail-fast.mjs`
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-arg-filtering.mjs`
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-merge-guard.mjs`

## Dependencies

None — created before the implementation children (test-first ordering).

## Deliverables

- New regression test file covering parent AC1, AC2, AC4 and AC5.

data.comment:
Implementation started (scope decision recorded).

**Scope decision — planning assumption (a).** The intake OPEN QUESTION asked whether this item should own the full end-to-end fix or only the notifier-side defence-in-depth. Planning assumed (a) and wired dependencies accordingly. Proceeding with (a): the wrapper-side fixes for the same root defect already landed via the sibling child SA-0MV13B4YT0093CKT — current `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` already has the fail-fast `parseReleaseArgs`, the pre-run `snapshotReleaseTags` gate (exit 14) and the `--help`/`unknown-flag` handling — so AC1/AC2/AC3 are satisfied end-to-end by that sibling. This item therefore delivers the unique remaining increment: **AC5** (notifier provenance guard) plus the Discord-specific regression test (AC4). No sibling work is duplicated.

**Design.** `sendReleaseNotification(release, options)` now accepts `options.preRunTags` (the pre-run `git tag --list` snapshot captured by the wrapper) and/or `options.tagCreatedByThisRun`. A new exported `isVersionTagNew(version, provenance)` helper decides provenance conservatively: an explicit `false` flag, a `null` snapshot (fail closed), or the presence of `v<version>` in the snapshot all refuse; otherwise the tag is treated as this run's. The guard runs **before** the webhook is resolved and before any payload is built, returning `{ success: true, notified: false, skipped: true, reason: 'version tag not created by this run' }`, so no POST is ever attempted. `run-release.js` Step 8.5 forwards `{ preRunTags }`. Legacy callers that omit provenance are unaffected (the guard is not applicable).
